🇲🇽🏭 DESPITE TARIFFS, MEXICO SETS AN EXPORT RECORD AND IS NOW THE US'S #1 SUPPLIER

Mexico shipped $54.18 billion to the United States in May — the highest single month ever recorded, up 17.5% year-on-year (US Census Bureau). It now accounts for 17.4% of all US imports, ahead of Canada (11.7%), China (7.5%) and Germany (4.3%), with $558 billion in sales over the last 12 months. The tariffs meant to punish Mexico left it as America's single largest trading partner.

🔥🇲🇽 MEXICO BARS TWO FIRMS FROM FEDERAL CONTRACTS FOR FAKING BIDS

The Secretariat of Anti-Corruption and Good Governance sanctioned two companies for lying in federal tenders. Impulsora Cordobesa faked three contracts to inflate its experience while bidding to supply food to IMSS clinics — a 643,188-peso fine and a one-year ban; a second firm was barred three months for a bad-faith bid on motorcycle helmets. Both now sit in the public Directory of Sanctioned Providers.

🚨🇲🇽 UNAM FILES CRIMINAL COMPLAINT OVER ENTRANCE-EXAM FRAUD SCHEME

Mexico's national university filed a criminal complaint on July 3 after detecting operators selling families false guarantees of admission to its undergraduate programs — conduct UNAM says "could constitute crimes." This cycle 158,712 aspirants sat the exam; results publish July 17. Predators charging for a public education the state provides free by right.

🇲🇽⚽ MEXICO–ENGLAND IS NOW THE MOST-WATCHED BROADCAST OF THE CENTURY IN MEXICO

60 million people watched the Round-of-16 match at a packed Estadio Azteca — the biggest television audience in Mexico this century, past even the World Cup opener's 54 million. More than 80,000 filled the stadium Mexico is co-hosting in 2026. England took the game 3-0; the number that stands is the crowd that showed up for it.

🔥🇲🇽 SALINAS PLIEGO'S TV AZTECA DECLARED INSOLVENT — 23.3 BILLION PESOS IN DEBT

A federal judge placed Ricardo Salinas Pliego's TV Azteca into concurso mercantil on July 7, ruling the network insolvent with 1,970 unpaid debts totaling 23,345 million pesos — 147% more than it owed in 2022. The billionaire who spent years attacking the 4T from his own airwaves now has up to 365 days to negotiate with creditors or fall into bankruptcy. Among them: New York bondholders demanding $663 million unpaid since 2021.

🇲🇽🏭 US SWALLOWS 76% OF MEXICO'S CAR EXPORTS AS JUNE SHIPMENTS DROP 9.2%

Mexican light-vehicle exports fell 9.2% in June year-on-year, INEGI reported, with the United States absorbing 75.9% of everything Mexico shipped abroad in the first half of 2026 — one buyer taking three-quarters of the market, fully exposed to Trump's tariff swings. The case for trade diversification isn't ideological anymore, it's arithmetic.

🇲🇽📈 MEXICO #2 IN THE OECD FOR REAL WAGE GROWTH — AHEAD OF THE US AND CANADA

Mexican workers' real wages rose 15.1% since 2021 — more than triple the 4.9% OECD average — putting Mexico second among all member states behind only Slovenia, while the US and Canada saw real wages fall, per the OECD. The driver: relentless minimum-wage hikes under AMLO and Sheinbaum that neoliberal economists swore would destroy jobs.

🚨🇲🇽 SUPREME COURT TAKES UP AYOTZINAPA — TRUTH COMMISSION ON THE LINE

Mexico's Supreme Court voted 8-0 to review whether a federal court can order an independent Truth Commission to investigate the 2014 disappearance of the 43 Ayotzinapa students — a commission the FGR has resisted. Twelve years on, the fight over who controls the investigation, and whether victims get a seat at the table, reaches the highest court in the country.

🇲🇽🌎 NO APOLOGY, NO RELATIONS: MEXICO HOLDS THE LINE ON ECUADOR

Sheinbaum reaffirmed Mexico will not restore diplomatic ties with Ecuador until Quito formally apologizes for storming Mexico's embassy and dragging out asylee Jorge Glas by force — a flagrant breach of the Vienna Convention. "Otherwise, it becomes very complex," she said, with Mexico's case against Ecuador still live at the International Court of Justice.

🇲🇽☀️ MEXICO PUTS FREE SOLAR PANELS ON WORKING-CLASS ROOFS

Sheinbaum's "Sol del Norte" program is installing 5,500 rooftop solar panels on Mexicali's most vulnerable homes at zero cost to families — put up in a single day and cutting electricity bills up to 70% in a city of brutal summers. It's a 200-million-peso CFE investment, already expanding to Hermosillo, with 150,000 homes targeted nationwide across the sexenio.
